LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 TENSE: FUTURE TIME USING WILL/SHALL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Which words do we use to show future time? 2. How do you tell that something will happen in the future?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify words that indicate future time using will and shall in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use will and shall to express future time correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. collaborate with others to determine the correctness and appropriateness of the tense used in own or provided texts. Learner is guided to: • Pick sentences which express future time from a text. • Make sentences from a substitution table, • Answer questions on future time using will/shall collaboratively. • Construct sentences using will/shall collaboratively. 1. Which words do we use to show future time? 2. How do you tell that something will happen in the future? 60 • Role play activities they plan or wish to do in future with peers. • Watch videos offline or online and identify sentences featuring future time with peers, Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light • Use computers, tablets or mobile phones to listen to audio materials featuring future time Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or be supported by peers, learner support or teacher to use the devices. 61 • Make predictions (events, weather among other

Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or be supported by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to create the display charts. Core Competence developed: • Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner expresses future plans using will and shall in pairs. • Self-Efficacy is developed as the learner acquires the skill of making sentences about activities they plan do in future.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
